before: A local variable is a name for a value in this part of the Ruby program. score = 3 assigns the number 3 to score.
Reassigning with score = 8 replaces the earlier value; the name stays score.
puts score displays the current value. puts "score" displays the letters because the quotes make text.
Unquoted whole numbers are integers. For these examples, changing a variable does not change text already printed.
Expected result: 8. Follow the instructions in order; this is a worked example, not an in-app execution.
after: A variable is a name for a value you can use later.
Here score first refers to three. The next assignment changes what score refers to.
Give the name score the new value eight.

Follow the labeled parts of this example.
```ruby
score = 3
score = 8
puts score
```
The output is `8`. Puts reads the most recent score.
